description: This pie chart visually represents the distribution of mathematical problem types within the Odyssey Math dataset, categorized by subject and educational level. The chart is divided into ten distinct slices, each corresponding to a specific mathematical topic and its associated difficulty tier. The largest segment, colored dark blue, represents “Algebra – High School” at 17.83% (69 problems). The second largest, in coral pink, is “Pre-Calculus – High School” at 14.21% (55 problems). Other significant segments include “Combinatorics – Olympiad-level” at 9.56% (37 problems), “Geometry – Olympiad-level” at 6.46% (25 problems), and “Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level” at 6.46% (25 problems). Smaller segments include “Geometry – High School” at 3.62% (14 problems), “Differential Equations – University-level” at 3.62% (14 problems), “Calculus and Analysis – University-level” at 6.20% (24 problems), “Probability – University-level” at 5.43% (21 problems), “Statistics – University-level” at 4.39% (17 problems), and “Number Theory – Olympiad-level” at 1.03% (4 problems). Each slice is labeled with its full name, educational level, percentage, and the exact number of problems it contains. The chart appears to be sorted in descending order of percentage size, with the largest slice positioned at the bottom left and the smallest at the top left. There is no legend, and all percentage and count data are provided directly on the chart via labels extending from each slice.
